newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens on surge in demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens on surge in demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling lost ground against the dollar on Thursday shedding 10 cents on a large dollar buying order, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling commercial mean of 53.67 against the dollar from 53.57 on Wednesday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean of 88.41 from 88.72.
"There was a large buying order that came into the market on Wednesday which caused a slight ripple in the market," a dealer from a leading bank told Reuters.

Dealers said despite dollar inflows from exporters, a lot traders were in short dollar positions which even the supply could not match: "In fact we've got orders from importers not to buy until the shilling firms a little bit, but it does not look very likely. The underlying tone still remains weak," one said.
The money market remained tight with overnight rates quoted at 17-18 percent unchanged.
